newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds broadly unchanged in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds broadly unchanged in sluggish trade.

text.p: Irish bonds were broadly unchanged in sluggish trade on Tuesday as markets retreated after yesterday's burst of exuberance, dealers said.

"People have stepped back today and volumes have fallen away," one dealer said. "The view is still that we're in a bear phase and no one's quite sure how long it will last or whether convergence or EMU will come to the rescue."
Irish bonds had firmed on Monday in line with other European markets, boosted by weekend signals of a softening in Germany's stance on the EMU entry criteria.

On Tuesday, Irish bonds were underperforming against bunds on the short end of the curve, dealers said. The 10-year spread over bunds was at 90 basis points, while the five-year pick-up was at 145 basis points.
Looking ahead, dealers said the market awaited Irish March consumer prices data on Thursday and the release of U.S. March retail sales figures on Friday.
Markets are still nervous about the possibility of higher U.S. interest rates and this continues to undermine sentiment.

By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down three pence from Monday's close at 101.65 to yield 6.06 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 10 pence from the close at 108.05 to yield 6.80 percent.
Ireland's National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) said on Tuesday that it would auction 150 million Irish pounds of the eight percent Treasury bond due 2006 in a competitive auction on April 15.
Dealers said they expected the market to show "appetite" for the bonds.
"That area of the curve has been performing well in recent weeks," one dealer said. "The only negative is that the 10-year has cheapened up, but if you believe in EMU it's a good buy."
